body_markdown:
**Higher interest rates can slow investment. Patent expirations don't wait.**


One of the pharmaceutical industry's biggest challenges is approaching: a wave of blockbuster drugs losing patent protection and market exclusivity.


When that happens, lower-cost generics and biosimilars can enter the market, potentially eroding sales of established medicines.


For major pharmaceutical companies, the challenge is straightforward:


**Where will the next generation of revenue come from?**


Increasingly, part of the answer appears to be biotechnology innovation.


According to


****[J.P. Morgan's Q3 2026 Biopharma Report](https://www.jpmorgan.com/insights/markets-and-economy/outlook/biopharma-medtech-deal-reports?_hsmi=373453708&utm_source=chatgpt.com) **,** the industry recorded:


-


**$138.9 billion** in announced M&A across 113 transactions through September.


-


**$221.1 billion** in announced research and development licensing value, although only 6% represented upfront cash.


-


**$7.5 billion** raised through 22 biotech IPOs, surpassing full-year IPO totals for each year from 2022 through 2025.


These figures suggest that strategic capital continues flowing toward innovation, even in a challenging financing environment.


###


The Interest Rate Paradox


Higher borrowing costs can pressure smaller biotechnology companies, particularly those without commercial revenue that depend on external financing.


Yet established pharmaceutical companies face a different challenge.


**They need to replenish pipelines, replace revenue exposed to patent expirations, and secure promising technologies before competitors do.**


Acquisitions and licensing agreements can help accomplish those objectives without requiring every new treatment to be developed internally.


That doesn't mean every biotech company becomes an acquisition target. Clinical failures, regulatory uncertainty, financing constraints, and acquisition premiums remain substantial risks.


###


The Bigger Picture


The patent cliff is more than a pharmaceutical industry problem. It may represent a multiyear catalyst for investment, partnerships, and acquisitions across biotechnology.


**The takeaway:** Interest rates influence the cost of capital. Patent expirations influence the need for innovation.


And that need may prove to be one of biotech's most durable structural tailwinds.
